title: Integration Basics - Quiz
description: Test your understanding of integration basics concepts in PEGA

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of REST connectors in PEGA?
options: To integrate with external RESTful web services
questions.explanation: REST connectors integrate with external RESTful web services, enabling PEGA applications to consume and interact with external APIs and services.

questions.question: When should you use SOAP connectors instead of REST?
options: When integrating with legacy systems that only support SOAP
questions.explanation: SOAP connectors should be used when integrating with legacy systems that only support SOAP, as REST is generally preferred for modern integrations.

questions.question: How do you handle authentication in integrations?
options: Through secure authentication methods like OAuth, JWT, or API keys
questions.explanation: Authentication in integrations should use secure methods like OAuth, JWT tokens, or API keys, with proper credential management and security best practices.

questions.question: What is the benefit of connection pooling?
options: It improves performance by reusing existing connections
questions.explanation: Connection pooling improves performance by reusing existing connections, reducing connection establishment overhead and improving resource utilization.

questions.question: How should you handle integration failures?
options: Through comprehensive error handling, retry mechanisms, and fallback strategies
questions.explanation: Integration failures should be handled through comprehensive error handling, retry mechanisms with exponential backoff, and fallback strategies to ensure business continuity.

questions.question: What is the purpose of data mapping in integrations?
options: To transform data between different formats and structures
questions.explanation: Data mapping transforms data between different formats and structures, ensuring compatibility between PEGA and external systems during integration.

questions.question: When should you use file listeners?
options: For batch processing of files and legacy system integration
questions.explanation: File listeners are used for batch processing of files and legacy system integration, monitoring directories for new files and processing them automatically.

questions.question: How do you monitor integration performance?
options: Through comprehensive logging, metrics, and real-time monitoring
questions.explanation: Integration performance should be monitored through comprehensive logging, metrics collection, real-time dashboards, and alerting systems to ensure reliability.
